The most important thing is to start the SDK as soon as possible in your app flow. The reason is that when your app will send an URL request to your server before the SDK was started, then the request will not include the SDK’s HTTP headers. inlineContent.text: The SDK adds its HTTP headers to your URL requests automatically. There is no need to manually add those headers.

In Android, there are few cases which the challenge will be cancelled:
The user press on the device’s physical back button.
Other activity in your app is starting (which caused the challenge activity to be paused).

After the challenge is cancelled, the user will have to perform the action again. Then, a new challenge will appear. On both iOS and Android, your app should handle the “challenge was cancelled” result.

Whenever the new state fires, the SDK also writes the following info log so host-side log scrapers can rely on the exact wording:

— the user appears to have solved the challenge but a connectivity issue (captive portal, VPN, proxy, MITM tooling, or pinning failure) prevented the SDK from reaching the server to finalize the pass. Ask the user to retry on a different connection (e.g. switch from Wi-Fi to cellular) or disable the VPN/proxy. Treat this like a transient network failure: a retry may well succeed.
